question_text: P10,000 is placed in a time deposit earning 5% per year compounded annually. How much after 2 years?

hint_ladder.title: Unang Taon: Tubo ni Aling Nena
hint_ladder.text: Sa unang taon, ang P10,000 ay kumita ng 5% interest: P500. Balanse ay P10,500.

hint_ladder.title: Ikalawang Taon: Compound na!
hint_ladder.text: Ang susunod na interes ay sa P10,500 na kinikita, hindi sa P10,000. Dito pumapasok ang compounding.

hint_ladder.title: Multiply: P10,500 × 1.05
hint_ladder.text: I-multiply ang bagong balanse sa 1.05: P10,500 × 1.05 = P11,025.

hint_ladder.title: Sagot: P11,025
hint_ladder.text: Gamit ang formula: P10,000 × (1.05)^2 = P11,025. Mas mataas ng P25 kaysa simple interest.

A.text: You might have chosen A because you only computed the first year’s interest without compounding.

B.text: You might have chosen B because you treated the interest as simple: 5%×2=10% of principal.

C.text: Correct. After compounding, the amount is P11,025—computed as P10,000 × (1.05)^2.

D.text: You might have chosen D because you overestimated the compounding effect, perhaps using (1.05)^2=1.125.

next_time_rule: Key Takeaway: Compound interest—'tubo ng tubo'—gamit ang A = P(1+r)^t. Patong-patong ang interest, kaya mas mabilis lumaki kaysa simple.
deconstruct_text:
Si Aling Tinay, may-ari ng sari-sari store, nagdeposito ng P10,000 sa time deposit sa bangko. 5% per year compounded annually. Gusto niyang malaman kung magkano after 2 years, para mapambili ng bagong paninda.

Sa unang taon, ang tubo ay 5% ng P10,000 = P500, kaya naging P10,500 ang pera niya. Dito na pumapasok ang 'compounding'—sa ikalawang taon, ang tubo ay kikitain sa bagong balance na P10,500.

Kaya P10,500 × 1.05 = P11,025. Kaya ang sagot: P11,025. Hindi P10,500 (isang taon lang), hindi P11,000 (simple interest na 10%), at hindi P11,250 (overestimated compound).
